resources.string: A single with just one empty cell left in a row, column or box.
Includes Hidden Single (Box) and Hidden Single (Line). Crosshatching is one way to spot it.
A Naked Pair shared by a line and a box. This is different from a Pointing Pair, which concerns one digit.
A Naked Triple shared by a line and a box. This is different from a Pointing Triple, which concerns one digit.
Locked Candidates: box to line. Pair and Triple count positions of one digit, not different digits.
Locked Candidates: line to box. Pair and Triple count positions of one digit, not different digits.
Simple Coloring: color trap. An outside candidate sees both colors.
Simple Coloring: color wrap. Two candidates of the same color conflict.
An extension of Simple Coloring that also links the two candidates inside a bivalue cell.
A restricted 3-Y-Wing and a short XY-Chain.
An unrestricted 3-Y-Wing: the shared elimination digit is also in the pivot.
Uses the Sudoku Coach n-Y-Wing definition. From size 5 onward, the common letter-named wings and ALS-XZ have different scopes; they are not aliases.
A separately named form of X-Chain, using only one digit.
A closed form of XY-Chain, using bivalue cells.
Extends X-Chain by treating several positions for one digit as a single logical group.
A specific BUG-family deduction. BUG means Binary Universal Grave; BUG+1 has one extra candidate.
